A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Text4Seg and contain readable main text, tables, figures, and complete appendices. Renumbered appendices and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original segmentation, referring-expression comprehension, and visual-understanding results, together with ablations and qualitative examples in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds evaluations of CRF refinement and unrefined predictions across multiple backbones and tasks.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 and Figure 5 add CRF as an optional alternative to SAM for refining predicted masks. Semantic descriptors, R-RLE, LoRA training, the autoregressive objective, and the SAM refinement procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: The datasets and task coverage remain unchanged: RES/GRES/REC, visual understanding, and open-vocabulary segmentation use the same data. Appendix B's additional dataset lists document comparator training data; they do not establish new Text4Seg coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds HIPIE, PolyFormer-L, and UNINEXT-L to the RES comparison and removes LAVT there, while retaining LAVT in the GRES comparison. Table 3 adds PolyFormer-L for REC. The main MLLM comparator sets otherwise remain intact.

E3.justification: Additional comparisons introduce CRF refinement conditions and extend 32×32 InternVL2 evaluation to GRES and REC. The existing splits, metrics, backbone sizes, and training budgets are retained. The 32×32 RES evaluation already appeared in v1.

E4.justification: v1 already studies descriptor resolution, SAM variants, and RLE. v2 substantially extends refinement analysis: Tables 12–14 compare unrefined and SAM outputs across six backbones and three tasks, add CRF comparisons for RES/GRES, and examine 32×32 descriptors on GRES/REC. These additions more systematically isolate performance attributable to refinement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Most shared benchmark scores are retained, but substantial results are added for refinement variants and new comparators. For example, v2 retains InternVL2's GRES average of 71.1 with SAM and adds 64.9 without refinement and 67.3 with CRF. Table 6 also changes SAM-H cIoU from 79.3 to 79.2, although appendix Table 11 retains 79.3.

T1.justification: The semantic-descriptor construction and R-RLE reasoning remain unchanged. No formal assumptions, mathematical definitions, derivations, or proofs are substantively revised; CRF is introduced without new mathematical development.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about text-as-mask segmentation, architectural compatibility, 16×16 descriptors, state-of-the-art performance, and R-RLE's 74% compression and approximately threefold speedup.

C2.justification: New Appendix D.3 explicitly acknowledges that unrefined RES predictions lag LISA and GSVA and discusses mitigation through CRF or higher descriptor resolution. Section 4.3 shifts the REC explanation toward instruction following and visual grounding. Appendix B adds a more explicit argument about training-data comparability.

D1.justification: Tables 1–3 newly identify underlying LLMs, Table 4 explains LISA's mixed training data, and Appendix B details comparator CPT/SFT datasets. Text4Seg's training hyperparameters, SAM prompting steps, instruction templates, and repository link are retained. CRF configuration details are not supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to dense CRF inference, SmooSeg, PolyFormer, HIPIE, and SegLLM, while removing the mPLUG-Owl2 discussion and reference. Appendix B expands comparison of training requirements, but the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local edits clarify Figure 3's 6×6 illustration and condense several passages. A training-data comparison appendix and refinement discussion are added, renumbering existing appendices. The main narrative remains largely intact; the publication header and acknowledgment are also updated.

P2.justification: The quantitative presentation expands substantially: Tables 1–3 gain LLM columns, variant markers, and additional rows, while new appendix tables organize training-data comparisons and refinement results. Figure 5 adds CRF, and retained Figures 15–16 share a page. Existing plots and qualitative examples are largely preserved.

improvement.justification: v1 already examined SAM dependence, but v2's broader refinement comparisons and explicit backbone/training-data disclosures make the evidence easier to assess. These provide a useful extension without fundamentally changing the supported conclusions. The gain is limited by missing CRF configuration details and unresolved numerical inconsistencies, including the SAM-H values in Tables 6 and 11.
